name: Sn42Bi58 low-temp
reference: Chip Quik NC191LTA10 (Bi57Sn42Ag1, mp 137 C); 165-180 C peak per common SnBi practice
notes: For heat-sensitive parts. A 170 C peak keeps the package about 80 C below the 250 C absolute maximum a part like the TE MS5525DSO specifies, and clear of softening plastic barbs. THE DOOR MUST BE OPENED AT PEAK. SnBi melts at 138 C, and this oven cools at only about -0.2 C/s there with the door shut, so the tail above liquidus is set by the cooldown rather than by the profile: shut-door cooling gives over 150 s above liquidus against the 60-90 s this alloy wants, and the excess promotes brittle intermetallic growth. Door-open cooling was measured at -5 to -7 C/s; the tail here assumes a conservative -2.5 C/s. SnBi is brittle and should not be mixed with heavily SAC-plated finishes, so it suits a part fitted on its own rather than a whole board.
